title: The Chess Game Restarts
next_chapter_hook: Atop the imperial city, Chen Ji overlooked the chess game of the world, unaware that those eyes transcending heavenly dao were slowly opening from the void—the 49th chess piece had begun to develop its own will.

text.content: The phoenix carriage swayed gently, golden silk curtains fluttering in the morning breeze. Chen Ji gazed down at the golden-threaded phoenix token in his palm, his fingertips touching the cold metal, an unfamiliar excitement quietly burning in his chest. Princess Taiping's summons had come three days earlier than he anticipated. This token was a pass to the core of the imperial city, and also a new starting point for his scheme across the world. The identity of 'Master Longyuan,' after three years of hiding, was finally about to step into the light. Outside the window, the majestic imperial city loomed, the double-eaved Taihe Hall gleaming golden under the morning sun, like a slumbering beast slowly opening its eyes.

The moment he entered the Fengyi Palace, Chen Ji concealed all his edge. His pace was neither fast nor slow, his spine slightly hunched, perfectly portraying a frail hermit. Princess Taiping sat at the main seat, her purple palace attire making her sharp features even more commanding. She examined this legendary old man who could 'reverse fate and change destiny,' a playful smile curling at her lips: 'Master Longyuan, this palace has heard you can peer into heavenly secrets—might you be of use to this palace?' Chen Ji slowly raised his head, his turbid eyes meeting hers, and his aged voice carried an undeniable composure: 'What the princess requires, the heavenly secrets shall present.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji accepted the tea cup but did not rush to drink. He swept his gaze across the palace maids and eunuchs standing in attendance, and from the depths of his aged eyes flickered a cold intent—among these seemingly ordinary servants, three were clearly Han Lie's informants. He feigned an inadvertent cough and spoke in a hoarse voice: 'This old man observed the night sky and saw the Ziwei Star moving eastward. His Highness the Crown Prince will inevitably face a calamity within three months. The light version is demotion, the heavy version... separation of head from body.' The moment his words fell, the tea cup in Princess Taiping's hand nearly slipped. The temperature in the palace plummeted, and those 'informants' breathing grew noticeably more hurried. 'Does the master have a solution?' Princess Taiping's voice remained steady, but Chen Ji could hear the suppressed urgency. 'A solution?' Chen Ji's aged laughter echoed through the palace, 'Since this old man dared to come, naturally I came prepared.'

text.content: On the day of the imperial grand ceremony, the Tianqing Sect Mountain Gate opened wide. Hundreds of officials gathered, ten thousand citizens came to pay homage, and dragon banners fluttered violently before the Taihe Hall. Chen Ji, under the identity of 'Master Longyuan,' was invited by the Crown Prince to host the Heaven-Worshipping Ceremony. As he slowly climbed the altar leaning on his cane, countless gazes focused on him—some curious, some contemptuous, some scrutinizing, and most questioning: what right did this decrepit old man have to preside over such a grand ceremony? Chen Ji stood at the apex of the altar, overlooking the sea of black-clad crowd below. Morning light pierced through the clouds, gilding him in a golden rim. He slightly raised his head, that faint smile at the corner of his lips, and his silver hair scattered by the wind, all resembling someone long departed.

dialogue.content: 'Long live the Emperor—' Chen Ji's aged voice echoed before the Taihe Hall, 'Today we worship heaven, following the mandate of heaven.' Before his words finished, the jade talisman hidden in his sleeve quietly shattered. A beam of light invisible to the naked eye shot toward the clouds, and in an instant, the originally clear sky faintly manifested a virtual image of a golden dragon! Officials clamored, citizens knelt in worship, and even the emperor on the high platform could not help but stand. 'The dragon... dragon vein manifests! This is an auspicious omen!' The Minister of Rites was so excited his old tears flowed. Chen Ji lowered his gaze, watching all this, a cold smile in his heart—this was merely a decoy he exchanged with his Heavenly Fate Value, the true killing move was still to come. 'Your Highness the Crown Prince,' he turned to the tall figure beside him, his aged voice carrying undeniable authority, 'please step forward to receive the decree.'

After the ceremony concluded, the Crown Prince invited Chen Ji into the Eastern Palace's secret chamber. The moment the chamber doors closed, Chen Ji's hunched spine slowly straightened. He casually tore off the aged mask on his face, revealing a young yet composed visage—precisely the 'dead' Chen Ji. The Crown Prince's pupils slightly contracted, then burst into hearty laughter: 'Master Longyuan plays an excellent role! But can this 'dead man's' identity truly deceive the world?' Chen Ji stored the mask in his sleeve, calmly gazing at the Crown Prince: 'Your Highness's enemies are currently troubling themselves over this. Within three days, Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie will definitely make a move. At that time, Your Highness only needs to follow the current.' He took out a sealed letter from his chest, 'Here are the evidences of Han Lie colluding with the northern barbarians. Please examine it, Your Highness.' The Crown Prince's expression instantly turned grim, his fingers slightly trembling as he took the letter. Chen Ji turned to gaze out the window, where lay the most prosperous Zhuque Street of the imperial city. 'The good show has just begun.'

text.content: Han Lie came calling on the seventh day. The number one prodigy of the Xuanwu Sect kicked open the inn's main door, his spear sweeping across, shattering Chen Ji's arranged formations. His entire body radiated killing intent, his eyes burning with undisguised fury: 'Chen, you think changing your disguise can cover your tracks?' Chen Ji sat calmly behind the table, his teacup perfectly still. He raised his eyes to look at this former nemesis, a trace of mockery flickering in his gaze: 'Young Master Han, traveling all this way, just to spout a few meaningless words?' Han Lie's forehead veins bulged, his spear pointing directly at Chen Ji's throat: 'You framed my Xuanwu Sect disciples, colluded with the imperial family, today I will cleanse the sect for you!' However, just as the spear was about to touch Chen Ji, a cold voice rang out from outside the door—

dialogue.content: 'Han Lie, you dare!' Su Qingyao, dressed in white, entered sword in hand. Her beautiful face frost-laden, she stood before Chen Ji, the tip of her sword pointing directly at Han Lie's brow: 'Inner Disciple Senior Fellow Su Qingyao of the Tianqing Sect is here—if you so much as touch a hair on him, you make an enemy of the entire Tianqing Sect!' Han Lie laughed out of fury: 'Su Qingyao, a堂堂 Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, actually protecting atrash?' A complex emotion flickered in Su Qingyao's eyes, but she did not retreat: 'trash? He was already a successor disciple designated by the sect elders three years ago. If you don't believe it, you may ask Sect Master Ling Yuan.' Han Lie's expression slightly changed, clearly not expecting this layer of complication. In the moment of his hesitation, Chen Ji slowly rose from his seat, walking to Su Qingyao's side. His voice was terrifyingly calm: 'Young Master Han, you led people to storm the imperial inn at night, threatened a Tianqing Sect elder's successor disciple with weapons—this account will greatly interest the imperial city's guards.' He lightly clapped twice, and instantly dozens of black-armored guards surged forth from all around the inn. Han Lie's expression thoroughly sank.

text.content: That night, Han Lie was detained by the guards on charges of 'private intrusion into the inn, attempted treason.' The Xuanwu Sect urgently sent people to bail him out, but the Crown Prince turned them back with 'evidence is conclusive, a thorough investigation is required.' Within three days, Han Lie's forces in the imperial city were uprooted, thirteen strongholds destroyed, and thirty-seven confidants arrested. The Xuanwu Sect's reputation plummeted, while the name 'Master Longyuan' was thoroughly established through this battle. The Crown Prince gazed at the mountain of reports on his desk, a hint of wariness flickering in his eyes. This seemingly frail strategist's methods were so ruthless—from the beginning, he never intended to give Han Lie any chance of a comeback. 'Master,' the Crown Prince put down the reports, his tone considerably more serious, 'what should we do next?'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji did not answer. His gaze passed through the Crown Prince, landing on a farther place. The burning sensation in his chest told him—the Tianji Record was stirring again. He made an excuse of physical discomfort, returned alone to the secret chamber, and sat cross-legged. Opening the palm that held the yellowed fragment, the originally blank fourth page was slowly revealing new text. The first line of words clearly read: 【Volume Seven Final Chapter·Death Prophecy—Number Delayed.】 Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. He stared at that line of text, his heart pounding like a war drum. Delayed? What does delayed mean? He continued reading: 【The true death prophecy lies in Volume Nine's final chapter.届时，天命者将面临最终抉择——是成为新的天道，还是化作天道养分。】 The text on the fourth page of the Tianji Record ceased abruptly, as if mocking his ignorance. Chen Ji slowly closed the book pages, his knuckles white from gripping. So from the beginning, everything had been under the gaze of that 'eye.'

text.content: The candlelight in the secret chamber flickered unstably, Chen Ji's shadow cast on the wall like a crouching beast. His breathing gradually steadied, the shock in those eyes replaced by something deeper. Delayed does not mean cancelled, merely postponed to a farther time node. This meant—he was still alive, could still scheme, could still resist. Master Mo's voice rang in his mind, carrying a hint of relief: 【Well done, the knowledge of the fourth page has been unsealed. Between Volume Seven and Volume Eight, you will gain more intelligence about the 'Eye of Heavenly Dao.'】 Chen Ji did not respond to Master Mo. He stood up and pushed open the window of the secret chamber. Outside, the countless lights of the imperial city spread like stars falling, and he, Chen Ji, stood at the center of it all. The feigned death was flawlessly concluded, the new identity commanded the undercurrents of the imperial dynasty. From chess piece to chess player, he had achieved it in merely one volume's time. 'But this is not enough,' he murmured, 'Han Lie is merely the beginning, Ling Yuan has yet to show his true fangs.' His hand stroked the burning sensation in his chest, 'And that eye... sooner or later, I will personally drag it down from the void.'

Three days later, the Crown Prince held a banquet to celebrate victory. Chen Ji put on the aged mask once more, attending as 'Master Longyuan.' At the banquet, he observed every person present without showing his feelings—opportunistic nobles, scheming sect disciples, and several top-tier experts with deeply concealed auras. Princess Taiping was also among them, her gaze occasionally falling on Chen Ji, carrying an inexplicable scrutiny. After several rounds of wine, Chen Ji excused himself and climbed alone to the highest point of the imperial city—the Xuantai Platform. This was the symbol of imperial power and the place where past emperors performed heaven-worshipping rituals. Night wind whistled, stirring his wide robes. Chen Ji overlooked this majestic imperial city beneath him, an unprecedented grandeur surging in his heart. Three years of scheming, thetrash persona, feigning death to escape, reappearing as 'Master Longyuan'—from today forward, he, Chen Ji, was no longer anyone's chess piece. 'The chess game of this world,' he spoke softly, his voice dispersed by the wind yet seeming to carry echoes, 'henceforth, I shall be the one to play.'

Meanwhile, thousands of miles away in the Tianqing Sect's Back Mountain, within a hidden cave dwelling. Master Mo's residual soul phantom floated in mid-air, staring at the cluster of faint light in his palm—the connection between him and Chen Ji. Outside the cave, the night was as ink, mountain winds mournful. Master Mo's form began to blur, as if it might dissipate at any moment. But in his turbid eyes burned a light almost like obsession. 'The good show has just begun,' he murmured, his voice seeming to come from antiquity, 'Number 49... no, it should be said, the Forty-Ninth Generation Heavenly Fate Holder. You adapted to the role of chess player faster than I anticipated.' He raised his head, as if he could penetrate the layers of mountains to see the direction of the imperial city. 'But the true test lies ahead. The Eye of Heavenly Dao has already noticed you—it does not like its chess pieces to have their own will.' Before Master Mo's form completely dissipated, a meaningful arc curled at the corner of his lips: 'But this is more interesting, isn't it?'

The instant Master Mo dissipated, Chen Ji clutched his chest suddenly. A strange chill crawled from his spine to the back of his skull, nearly causing him to stumble. He raised his head to gaze at the night sky, countless stars twinkling, seemingly ordinary. But his intuition told him—something was watching him from extremely high and far. That was the feeling of being stared at by a predator. Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. The Tianji Record fragment in his chest was slightly hot, as if responding to something. He did not use Tianji to peer into it, because he knew—some things were not what he could touch at present. 'Chen Nian...' he murmured this name, a rare gentleness flickering in his gaze. Sister, where are you? As long as you still exist, this game still has the most critical variable. The night wind of the imperial city howled past, dispersing Chen Ji's final hesitation. He turned and descended the Xuantai Platform, disappearing into the night. A new game had already begun.

choice.prompt: After the imperial ceremony concluded, the Crown Prince sought advice from 'Master Longyuan': Han Lie may be defeated, but the Xuanwu Sect's foundation remains intact—how should we completely dismantle their forces?

choices.text: Removing the Fuel from the Cauldron
choices.description: Using the evidence of Han Lie colluding with barbarians, unite other sects to pressure the Xuanwu Sect, forcing them to hand over Han Lie to prove their innocence.
choices.visible_cost: Deplete the Crown Prince's favors owed to the Xuanwu Sect
choices.visible_reward: The Xuanwu Sect splits, Han Lie completely loses power
choices.risk_hint: May escalate conflicts between sects and the imperial dynasty

text.content: The Crown Prince heard this and laughed heartily while applauding: 'Master's strategy is brilliant!' He immediately wrote several letters and sent them to major sects throughout the night. Within three days, the Xuanwu Sect was pushed to the eye of the storm, forced to proactively hand over Han Lie to appease public outrage. When the news reached the imperial city, Chen Ji was savoring his tea. He set down his teacup, a slight smile curling at his lips—Han Lie, this is merely the beginning.

Inside the Xuanwu Sect's great hall, Sect Master Han Xiaotian furiously threw Han Lie's crime confession to the ground. His face ashen, he gazed at his clan brother Han Lie kneeling in the hall, his voice cold as ice: 'From this day forward, you are no longer a disciple of the Xuanwu Sect. Life and death are each at fate's mercy.' Han Lie shuddered all over, raising his head to look at the figures behind the sect master—people from the Tianqing Sect, Star Pavilion, and Xuanming Valley, three major sects, all present. He knew he had been completely abandoned. And the mastermind behind all this, that old man called 'Master Longyuan'... He clenched his fists, nails deeply embedding into his palms, his eyes burning with deep-seated hatred. Imperial city, Chen Ji, I, Han Lie, will have an undying vendetta with you!

choices.description: Let the Crown Prince take the initiative to make overtures to the Xuanwu Sect, spare Han Lie, and exchange this for the Xuanwu Sect's covert support in the imperial war.
choices.visible_reward: The Xuanwu Sect secretly submits, the Crown Prince reaps the benefits
choices.risk_hint: Releasing a tiger back to the mountain brings endless troubles

text.content: The Crown Prince frowned slightly: "Sir, Han Lie is narrow-minded. Releasing him would be nurturing a tiger's harm, would it not?" Chen Ji shook his head with a faint smile: "Your Highness only needs to remember one thing—the enemy's enemy is a friend. Han Lie hates me, not Your Highness. If something changes in the future, Your Highness will be his only lifesaver." After contemplating for a moment, the Crown Prince finally nodded. Chen Ji gazed at the night outside the window, but in his heart was calculating something else: Han Lie, you are still useful. Before completely destroying the Xuanwu Sect, let you be arrogant for a few more days.

choices.description: Temporarily ease pressure on Han Lie, focus on supporting the Crown Prince to stabilize the court, secretly place pieces in the Xuanwu Sect, and wait for the right moment to strike fatally.
choices.visible_cost: Slow results, requires patience to wait
choices.visible_reward: The Crown Prince's position is stable, nails planted within the Xuanwu Sect
choices.risk_hint: During this period, Han Lie might discover the truth

text.content: Chen Ji handed a stack of names to the Crown Prince: "These people can be useful to Your Highness." The Crown Prince took a look, his pupils contracting sharply—the names on the list included three core elders of the Xuanwu Sect and five powerful disciples. "When did you..." Chen Ji cut him off: "Your Highness doesn't need to know too much. Just remember, these people will become stepping stones on Your Highness's path to the throne." The Crown Prince took a deep breath, his gaze toward Chen Ji now carrying genuine awe. This "Master Longyuan" was more profound than he had imagined. Three months later, when the Crown Prince successfully ascended the throne, he finally understood how terrifying Chen Ji's layout had been—the Xuanwu Sect had already been riddled with holes by his infiltration.

choice.prompt: The Tianji Record fourth page reveals a shocking truth: the death prophecy is merely delayed, the true ending prophecy points to Volume Nine. How should Chen Ji respond to this discovery?

choices.description: Using the identity and resources of "Master Longyuan" to accelerate the search for other fragments of the Tianji Record, attempting to complete the full version before the death prophecy arrives.
choices.visible_cost: May expose the existence of the Tianji Record, attracting more covetous pursuers
choices.visible_reward: The more fragments, the more knowledge unsealed, the greater the odds of victory
choices.risk_hint: Actions too bold will alarm the Heavenly Eye

text.content: Chen Ji immediately, in the name of "Master Longyuan," issued a hero's summons across the world: offering great rewards for purchase of Tianji treasures and rare ancient books. His movements were swift, swift enough to alarm even the Taiping Princess. "Sir, what are you searching for?" she probed. Chen Ji only smiled: "Just some old hobbies from my youth, nothing more." His tone was light, as if merely collecting some insignificant trinkets. However, he knew this was merely self-deception. The moment the fourth page of the Tianji Record appeared, he distinctly felt—the "eye" had moved. It was watching him. Like a hunter watching prey fallen into a trap, patient and cruel.

choices.description: Chen Nian is the "Heavenly Fate Key," her existence can disrupt the Tianji Record's foresight—and perhaps also disrupt the Heavenly Eye's surveillance.
choices.visible_cost: Divides energy, may alarm the prey
choices.visible_reward: Finding the key to resisting the Heavenly Eye
choices.risk_hint: Chen Nian is controlled by the Holy Sect, reckless action may harm her

text.content: Chen Ji picked up his pen and wrote two characters on paper: "Chen Nian." These two characters seemed to weigh a thousand tons, pressing down until he could barely breathe. He hadn't heard any news of his sister for three years. She had been taken by the Holy Sect as the "Heavenly Fate Key," supposedly capable of opening an ancient forbidden land. He could not sit and wait for death. He must find her. Even if it meant paying any price. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind, carrying a hint of solemnity: [Finding her might become the key to reversing fate. But you must prepare yourself—the waters of the Holy Sect run deeper than you imagine.] Chen Ji tucked the paper into his chest, a resolute light burning in his eyes. "Chen Nian, your brother is coming for you."

In a dense forest outside the imperial city, a girl in black纱 suddenly raised her head. Between her brows, a golden mark was faintly warming. "Brother..." she murmured, her voice scattered by the night wind. Chen Nian gazed toward the direction of the imperial city, and in those clear eyes, a complex light flickered. She didn't know how much longer she could hold on. The people of the Holy Sect used her blood every day to open the forbidden land, and her consciousness was being eroded bit by bit by some kind of power. But she knew, her brother would definitely come for her. He definitely would.

choices.description: Since escape is impossible, better to take the initiative. Using the Tianji Record's foresight ability, attempt to find the weaknesses of the Heavenly Eye.
choices.visible_cost: May anger the Heavenly Eye, bringing destructive retaliation
choices.visible_reward: May find the true method to break the situation
choices.risk_hint: The Heavenly Eye is the final BOSS, acting rashly is extremely dangerous

text.content: Chen Ji sat cross-legged, his palms open with the Tianji Record spread out. His gaze fell upon those words—【Volume 9 Final Chapter·Final Choice】. He closed his eyes, his consciousness sinking into that familiar chaos. This time, he didn't try to foresee the future, but gathered all his mental focus into a single thought: I know you're watching. What do you want? Silence. Endless silence. Just when Chen Ji thought he was merely talking to himself, an ancient and authoritative voice exploded in his mind: 【Interesting. Number 49... you've finally dared to face me directly.】 Chen Ji's soul felt like it had been struck by thunder, an indescribable fear instantly spreading through his entire body. He abruptly opened his eyes, finding himself drenched in sweat, and on the fourth page of the Tianji Record, in what was originally a blank corner, a new line of small characters had appeared: 【It has already seen you.】

Chen Ji stared at those words, his heart pounding like war drums. He knew that from this moment on, everything had changed. He was no longer a nameless nobody, no longer a dispensable chess piece—the Heavenly Eye had remembered him. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind, carrying rare gravity: 【You've made a very risky decision. But perhaps... this is the only correct path.】 Chen Ji slowly stood up and walked to the window. The night sky was filled with countless stars, but he couldn't shake the feeling that behind those stars, a pair of eyes was watching him. "Since you're watching," he said softly, his voice carrying a hint of madness, "then watch carefully. Watch how I, step by step, jump off your chessboard."

Meanwhile, in the depths of the Void. A massive eye slowly opened, its pupil reflecting Chen Ji's figure—or rather, reflecting that figure standing atop the imperial city, gazing up at the heavens. 【Number 49... no, it should be the 49th Generation Heavenly Fate Bearer.】 Its voice was like the great bells and thundering drums, echoing through the entire Void, 【Interesting. After all these years, finally one... dares to face me directly as a chess piece.】 It showed no anger, no threats, only... laughter. That smile sent chills down one's spine, for there was no emotion within it whatsoever, only pure, transcendent indifference. 【The good show has just begun.】

Chen Ji stood atop the imperial city, overlooking the city that determined the fate of the world below. The feigned death was perfectly executed, the new identity controlled the hidden currents of the dynasty, and the fourth page of the Tianji Record revealed deeper truths—but all of this was merely the beginning of a greater chess game. He knew that from this day forward, he was no longer the invisible chess playerscheme in secret, but a rebel standing on stage, playing against Heaven. The road ahead was treacherous, fate was uncertain, but so what? "I, Chen Ji, from waste to today, never relied on luck." He murmured softly, turning to descend the Xuanwu Terrace. The night wind howled, scattering his final words. A new game had begun. And he would hold the chess piece in hand, advancing methodically. Behind him, that eye transcending Heaven and Earth was opening from the Void, carrying an inexplicable interest—【Interesting, Number 49 has begun to resist.】

Princess Taiping stood before the window of the Fengyi Palace, the secret letter from the Xuanwu Sect clutched in her hand. Her gaze was deep and unfathomable, unreadable. After a moment, she set the letter ablaze, watching the flames consume the evidence of betrayal. "Lord Longyuan..." she murmured softly, "just who are you?" Just then, a maid rushed in and knelt: "Your Highness, His Majesty requests your presence." Princess Taiping straightened her appearance, resuming her dignified and commanding demeanor. As she walked toward the Imperial Study, her mind was calculating: the Crown Prince's enthronement was imminent, Lin Xiao of the Tianqing Sect's old Sect Master was about to exit seclusion, the Xuanwu Sect had been severely weakened... the game was becoming more and more interesting. And that mysterious "Lord Longyuan," were they friend or foe? "Interesting," she said, a slight smile curving her lips, "This palace shall see just how long this good show can last."

Tianqing Sect, Rear Mountain Forbidden Grounds. Lin Xiao sat cross-legged in the stone chamber of seclusion, wisps of Spiritual Energy swirling around him. His aura was more profound and restrained than three years ago, like an unfathomable abyss. Suddenly, he opened his eyes, and a sharp gleam flashed through those turbid old eyes. "Interesting," he murmured softly, "Chen Ji... you truly didn't die." He rose and pushed open the seal of the stone chamber. After three years of seclusion, he had finally touched that legendary realm. And his first thought was of that disciple he had once despised, now become a fatal threat—the "waste" disciple. "The inheritor of the Tianji Record..." Lin Xiao walked out of the stone chamber, gazing toward the direction of the imperial city, "This time, this old man will not miss the opportunity again." His voice was soft, yet carried undeniable resolve. Somewhere in the imperial city, in a hidden corner. A figure in night attire quietly appeared—it was Mo Xiansheng, the residual soul from the first page of the Tianji Record. His gaze penetrated the layers of night, falling upon that young figure atop the imperial city. "The good show has just begun," he murmured, "and this time, the audience... is not only you." He looked up toward the Void, as if he could see that eye awakening from the abyss, "The Heavenly Eye... it can no longer wait."

On this very night, the entire world subtly sensed some kind of change. Above the imperial city, the originally weak dragon vein energy suddenly intensified; in the Tianqing Sect Rear Mountain, a seal dormant for many years began to loosen; in the depths of the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, a imprisoned girl suddenly opened her eyes; and in the deepest part of the Void, that eye transcending Heaven and Earth finally opened completely. It reflected Chen Ji's figure, its pupil holding no emotion whatsoever, only pure, transcendent will. 【Number 49... no, it should be the 49th Generation Heavenly Fate Bearer.】 Its voice was like the great bells and thundering drums, echoing through the entire Void, 【After all these years, finally one... dares to face me directly as a chess piece.】 Chen Ji stood atop the imperial city, he could feel it—that sensation of being watched, clearer than ever before. But he felt no fear; instead, he smiled. "Watch closely," he said softly, "I will let you know what it means for a chess piece to rebel." A new game had begun. And this time, he would hold the chess piece in hand, reversing fate against Heaven!
